Q: How can different parts of a HTML Text node be formatted differently? A:

The formatting is coming from the font, not from the HTML or CSS splitting the text node.

The element contains only one text node:

<div class="ods-price__value">4.99*</div>

The site applies the custom LidlFontPricePublicBeta font to it. That font contains OpenType substitution rules that replace certain character sequences with alternative glyphs.

In particular, two digits following a decimal point are represented by smaller glyphs. So .99 is still ordinary text as far as the DOM is concerned; the font renderer simply selects different glyphs for those characters.

This is why removing the custom font makes the 9s appear at their normal size. It also explains why the behavior is specific to patterns such as .01–.99, without requiring separate <span> elements.

The effect is therefore encoded in the font's OpenType tables, most likely through contextual or ligature substitution.

Q: BLE requestConnectionPriority(HIGH) only helps one of two GATT links A:

Note that all Bluetooth controller chips on the market I'm aware of can only handle one radio channel at any given time. This means that it needs to time multiplex your two connections onto the same radio. You can thus physically not have two connections simultaneously at full performance. The Bluetooth controller will schedule the connections in an implementation-specific way. This scheduling is not standardised in the Bluetooth spec and there is no hci command to customise this, except for "connection event length", which Android did not use the last time I checked. The Bluetooth version is irrelevant for your question.

Q: Process finished with exit code 134 (interrupted by signal 6: SIGABRT) A:

This could be caused by a stack overflow; check your code for infinite recursions. Here's a minimal code example to reproduce:

import asyncio


async def foo():
    await foo()

asyncio.run(foo())

This results in:

Process finished with exit code 134 (interrupted by signal 6:SIGABRT)

Q: SqlBulkCopy invalid column length...but it's not A:

In my case the issue is Boolean type, Azure read my .dsv file, and understand that "f" or 0 in my columns its for false, so INT, or any string types is not actual for this column. I changed datatype of my sink column as BIT and its worked for me.
